title: Debugging in production without breaking it: `exec`, `port-forward` and ephemeral copies

videos.script: Lesson 40 read what the cluster says about a pod. Sometimes that is not enough, and you need to look inside. {{inside}} The obvious tool, a shell in the container, often does not exist: the shop's image has one program in it and nothing else. That is good for security and bad for curiosity. {{noshell}} Kubernetes has three better answers. Reach the pod from your laptop without exposing it. Attach a temporary container with tools, beside the one that has none. Or make a copy of a broken pod and take the copy apart, leaving the original alone. {{three}} Each of these changes as little as possible, and that is the rule in production. {{rule}}
